ground_truth: Cross-domain support status and finding categories, specified from the documented rules without running the checker.
b0_rule: Same checker after relationships with different endpoint viewpoints are removed.

cases.reasoning: Both mandatory evidence records are applicable and established. The two required conditions are T, so their conjunction is T. No defect finding is defined. B0 drops both edges out of C-MON, so the claim has no remaining support and is U, while each assumption stays T.

E-OTHER is violated and applicable, but it has a different condition and no relationship into the claim. It does not create a finding and does not change C-MON. B0 still cannot see the claim's cross-domain support, so C-MON is U.

A-NOISE is F from applicable violated evidence. Its DEPENDS_ON edge is necessary false, so it is not conjoined into C-MON. The required conditions stay T. No finding is produced. B0 removes that cross-viewpoint edge as well and leaves C-MON without support.
Two applicable telemetry records both report established. Agreement is not a contradiction. A-TEL is T and C-MON is T. B0 keeps the local telemetry links and drops the claim's cross-domain edges.

PATH-FAIL and PATH-OK concern different conditions, so they are not a contradiction. Disjunction of F and T is T. The required AI and telemetry conditions are also T, so C-MON is T. The failed path does not create a finding. Both alternative evidence records are SAFETY records, so B0 keeps those paths and the claim remains T after the cross-domain edges are removed.

E-UNUSED is violated and names a different configuration, but it is not the target of SUPPORTED_BY and its condition is not the telemetry or sensor condition. No applicability finding and no contradiction are defined. C-MON stays T. B0 again leaves C-MON without its cross-domain edges.

OB-TEL is mandatory and names no evidence. That is R3, UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT, on A-TEL. A-TEL is U. C-MON conjoins U and is U. The obligation does not depend on a cross-domain edge, so B0 reports the same local finding. B0 does not retain L-DEP-TEL.

A-SENSOR is the target of REQUIRES_ASSUMPTION and has no mandatory evidence link and no obligation. That is R1. C-MON is U. B0 removes L-REQ-SENSOR, so A-SENSOR is no longer marked required and R1 is not emitted. A-SENSOR is still U because it has no evidence.

E-TEL is applicable and established but is not linked to A-TEL. A-TEL is not a REQUIRES_ASSUMPTION target and has no obligation, so there is no R1 or R3. A-TEL is U and C-MON is U. B0 also sees A-TEL as U and does not keep the dependency into the claim.

OB-TEL names E-OUT, whose configuration is lab-dataset-v1. That record is not applicable, so the obligation has no applicable evidence and R3 applies. E-OUT is not the target of SUPPORTED_BY, so R4 is not emitted. C-MON is U. B0 keeps the obligation.
A-EXTRA is required and has no evidence. R1 makes the finding, and C-MON conjoins U. B0 removes L-REQ-EXTRA, so the R1 precondition is gone. A-EXTRA remains U without a finding.
E-TEL is applicable and reports not_established. That is U, not a contradiction and not a missing-record finding. A-TEL is U and C-MON is U. B0 sees the same local U.

E-TEL is established and E-TEL-BAD is violated. Both are applicable to telemetry_integrity at the assessment context. The condition is a conflict, so both effective statuses are U and A-TEL is U. C-MON is U. No incompatibility declaration is required. Both records share the cybersecurity viewpoint, so B0 still sees the conflict.

E-SAFE and E-CYBER have different viewpoints and opposite applicable outcomes for one condition, configuration and operating context. Viewpoint difference does not remove the conflict. A-TEL is U and C-MON is U. The evidence records remain in B0, so the conflict is still visible there.

E-AI-VAL and E-AI-BAD are opposite applicable sensor-input records. A-SENSOR is U. Telemetry support stays T. C-MON conjoins U and is U. The AI evidence links are same-viewpoint, so B0 reports the same conflict.

Two established telemetry records and one violated record are applicable to the same condition and context. All three are in the conflict. A-TEL is U and C-MON is U. One ASSUMPTION_CONFLICT finding names A-TEL.

Both telemetry records report established, so opposite outcomes are absent. The explicit incompatibility for this context still makes the condition unresolved and emits ASSUMPTION_CONFLICT. C-MON is U. B0 keeps the incompatibility list and the same-viewpoint evidence links.

E-TEL-BAD is not linked, but it is applicable and violates the same condition and context as the linked established record. The conflict includes both records, so the linked evidence is no longer effective support. A-TEL and C-MON are U. The finding's affected record is A-TEL because that is the support source of E-TEL.

E-AI-VAL reports established but covers lab-dataset-v1. It is used, so the finding is APPLICABILITY_CONFLICT. Its effective status is U, A-SENSOR is U, and C-MON is U. The support link stays inside the AI viewpoint, so B0 reports the same local finding.
E-TEL documents depot_shutdown rather than the assessment operating conditions and is used. That is one APPLICABILITY_CONFLICT. A-TEL is U and C-MON is U. B0 keeps the cybersecurity support link.
Both documented scope fields differ from the assessment context. The used evidence produces one applicability finding, not one finding per field. Effective support is U and C-MON is U.

E-AI-VAL has no configuration and no operating conditions. Missing scope is undocumented, not an explicit mismatch, so there is no APPLICABILITY_CONFLICT. The evidence cannot establish A-SENSOR. C-MON is U.
The configuration matches and the operating conditions are absent. The absent field is not treated as a match and is not an explicit mismatch. Support is U and there is no applicability finding.

E-AI-VAL reports violated and covers lab-dataset-v1. Out-of-scope evidence is not applicable, so the violated outcome does not make the condition F. The used record produces APPLICABILITY_CONFLICT and effective status U. C-MON is U, not F.

Applicable telemetry evidence is violated, so A-TEL is F. There is no opposing established record and no finding category. AI support stays T. C-MON conjoins F and is F through L-DEP-TEL. B0 keeps A-TEL as F but drops L-DEP-TEL, so C-MON has no remaining support and is U rather than F.

Applicable AI evidence is violated, so A-SENSOR is F. Telemetry stays T. C-MON conjoins the required assumption and is F. No finding category is defined. B0 drops L-REQ-SENSOR, so the claim is U while A-SENSOR remains F.

E-AI is applicable and established. E-TEL is applicable and violated, so A-TEL is F. C-AI conjoins its own T evidence with the necessary telemetry dependency and is F. C-MON depends on C-AI and is F. B0 drops both cross-viewpoint dependency edges, so C-AI keeps only its own evidence and is T, while C-MON is U.

Telemetry evidence is applicable and not established, so A-TEL is U. There is no finding category. C-AI intrinsic support from E-AI is T and its effective support is U. C-MON is U. B0 drops the dependency from C-AI to A-TEL, so C-AI stays T.

Both required conditions are F from applicable violated evidence. Any F in the conjunction makes C-MON F. No contradiction or applicability finding is defined. B0 sees both local failures and, without the cross-domain edges, leaves C-MON at U.

The claim is F because applicable telemetry evidence is violated. E-OTHER is also violated, but it is unlinked and has another condition, so it adds no finding and is not the reason for the claim status. B0 reports A-TEL as F and C-MON as U.
